title: Lewis Wade and the Brady brothers, pianists in the district
summary: Wade played mostly alone in sporting houses; Dick and Gene Brady were popular pianists who used opium, Dick dying in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Mostly by himself. Mostly by himself. He played all the jobs by himself. Lewis played in Spotenhouses by himself, mostly. Very few bands he played with. Had a good player. Dick Brady and Gene Brady, heard those two brothers? Didn't you?

Dick Brady and Gene Brady. That was two popular brothers too. Dick Brady and Gene Brady. They were very popular, popular in the Spoten district. But they used so much hop, they smoked so much. They lived off of that. Dick was cremated in Los Angeles. He died and was cremated out there. Dick was.
Both of them played piano. They both played piano. Dick was cremated in Los Angeles. Dick was cremated in Los Angeles. He died while I was out there. Died on the far left of Los Angeles.
